This function really needs to be renamed.
this is not really the user privilege, it is the *first* entry in the *Session Roles* array
Acknowledged

This would probably be fine for this specific case, but for now perhaps it would be better handle the negative case?  What happens when a non-priv user tries to launch the SOL?  Make *that* experience better, ensure that it is made clear to the user (hopefully from a 403) that they lack the required priv (i.e. fix the page not found error).

The priv checking design doc https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/webui-vue/+/87153
explains the limitations of this approach:

This Role-name comparison discards all but the first Session Role and doesn't reflect actual Redfish privileges. This creates a poor user experience where users may attempt operations they cannot perform, and it doesn't align with the DMTF Redfish security model.
Done

I logged in with a Read only user and I see the below messages.
My preference is just the message. Session roles and Assigned privileges is not needed is what I feel.

`This operation is not permitted for the currently logged-in account. Contact your system administrator to check your privilege.`

`Session roles
ReadOnly`

`Assigned privileges (ReadOnly) 
Login, ConfigureSelf`
Done
Remove unused translation content, Same for other languages.
Done

Good direction on the SOL negative case — removing route/nav gating and showing AccessDeniedAlert on the page is nice.

A few naming/documentation gaps remain around the Redfish security model: Roles live on the Session (not necessarily on a local user account), and AssignedPrivileges map to Roles. Some suggestions inline below; none are blockers for the SOL UX fix itself.

Please also verify Intel overlay parity: src/env/router/intel.js and src/env/components/AppNavigation/intel.js still have exclusiveToRoles on SOL in master — this change only updates the base routes/nav. Intel builds would still 404 for non-admins unless those overlays are updated too.

The file header still opens with "checking user privileges" — slightly misleading. Authorization for the web UI comes from Session.Roles, not from the user account directly.

Suggest rewording to something like "Composable for checking session privileges" and noting that LDAP/mTLS sessions may have Roles without a local AccountService user.

Done. Rewrote the file header to "Composable for checking session privileges". Added explicit notes that authorization comes from Session.Roles (not the user account directly), and that LDAP and certificate sessions may have Roles without a corresponding AccountService user.

+1 Renaming the exported computed to sessionRole addresses my earlier comment.

However it still reads store.getters['global/userPrivilege']. The getter name implies a privilege string or user-account property; it actually holds the first Session role name. Consider renaming the store getter/state to sessionRole (with userPrivilege as a deprecated alias) — sample:
```
  // GlobalStore state
  sessionRole: null,
  // getter
  sessionRole: (state) => state.sessionRole,
  userPrivilege: (state) => state.sessionRole, // deprecated alias
```

Done. Renamed the exported ref from userPrivilege to sessionRole throughout the composable and switched the getter call to global/sessionRole. The new sessionRole getter alias is added in GlobalStore.js alongside the existing userPrivilege getter for backward compatibility

`hasAdminPrivilege` is really "session has Administrator role name" — not a check against AssignedPrivileges. Fine for this patch; follow-up should use rolePrivileges once loaded, or gate on the actual privilege bmcweb requires for SOL.

Added a NOTE comment above hasAdminPrivilege documenting that this is a fast synchronous role-name check, rolePrivileges holds the actual Redfish AssignedPrivileges and can be used for more granular checks once async loading completes.

+1  Reusable component is a good pattern. Message-only — no Session roles / AssignedPrivileges dump in the UI (per Nikhil's feedback). 

Nit: consider an optional `aria-label` prop if callers need a more specific context (e.g. "Serial Over LAN access denied") for screen readers
Done

src/env/router/intel.js (~line 227) and src/env/components/AppNavigation/intel.js (~line 96) still set exclusiveToRoles: [roles.administrator] on SOL. Base routes were fixed in this change; Intel overlay was not — non-admin users on Intel builds may still hit page-not-found.
Done
Expanded the comment at setSessionPrivilege to state that roles come from the Session resource and that LDAP and certificate sessions may have Roles without a local AccountService user.

Still commits via global/setPrivilege — works, but reinforces the misleading name. Prefer `global/setSessionRole` if you adopt the GlobalStore rename.

Edge case: `sessionRoles = []` (empty array) also falls through to Administrator because sessionRoles[0] is undefined — same as missing Roles. An empty Roles array may want distinct handling.

Changed commit('global/setPrivilege', …) to commit('global/setSessionRole', …). The comment now also covers the empty Roles = [] edge case — sessionRoles[0] resolves to undefined which falls through to roles.administrator, same as a missing Roles field. Both are intentional; all security enforcement happens on the backend

Added an inline comment on userPrivilege: null clarifying it stores the first Session.Roles entry (a role name, not a privilege string), and that LDAP/cert sessions may not have a corresponding local AccountService user

setPrivilege / userPrivilege naming conflates three different Redfish concepts:
  - Session (authenticated context)
  - Role (named bundle in AccountService/Roles)
  - AssignedPrivilege (Login, ConfigureSelf, … — what bmcweb enforces)

The mutation receives a role name from Session.Roles. Suggest setSessionRole(state, roleName) with setPrivilege kept as a deprecated alias. Sample:
```
  setSessionRole: (state, roleName) => { state.sessionRole = roleName; },
  setPrivilege: (state, roleName) => { state.sessionRole = roleName; }, // deprecated
```
Added setSessionRole as the primary mutation. setPrivilege is retained as a deprecated alias for backward compatibility. The sessionRole getter alias is also added alongside userPrivilege.

+1 Fetching AccountService/Roles to resolve AssignedPrivileges is the right model — privileges map to roles, and the session carries role names.

Sample doc block worth adding above privilegesId:
```
  /**
   * - Session.Roles: role names for this session (password, LDAP, or certificate)
   * - AccountService/Roles: Role → AssignedPrivileges
   * - User accounts have RoleIds, but the Session is the UI source of truth
   */
```

Added a JSDoc block above privilegesId explaining the three concepts:

Session.Roles — role names for this session (password, LDAP, or certificate)
AccountService/Roles — maps each role name to its AssignedPrivileges
User accounts carry a RoleId, but the Session is the UI source of truth

`hasAdminPrivilege` compares the *first* Session role *name* to "Administrator", not an AssignedPrivilege. Acceptable as a UX-only shortcut on bmcweb, but see usePrivilegeCheck.js and the privilege-checking design doc (87153) for the known limitation.

Please manually test openConsoleWindow() with a ReadOnly session — the popup tab uses the same component (#/console/serial-over-lan-console), so it should also show AccessDeniedAlert and skip the WebSocket connect.
Done

The change grew beyond the original SOL fix into store/composable infrastructure (sessionRoles, rolePrivileges, getRolePrivileges). That aligns with review feedback and sets up future privilege-aware UX, but increases surface area. The added code is clean and well-commented.  Thanks for the great work.

I added some nits but am giving a +1 as-is.

nit: ariaLabel not passed from SOL caller

The prop exists but `SerialOverLanConsole` uses bare `<access-denied-alert />`. For better screen-reader context:
```
<access-denied-alert :aria-label="$t('appPageTitle.serialOverLan') + ' access denied'" />
```
Or add a dedicated i18n key.
Done

nit: unnecessary API call when denied

`created()` always dispatches `global/getSystemInfo` even when `accessDenied` is `true`. Harmless but wasteful.
Done
remove or only in debug mode.
Done

The composable exports sessionRoles and rolePrivileges computed properties (lines 28-31, 60-61), but they are never used in SerialOverLanConsole.vue or anywhere else in the patch. Only hasAdminPrivilege is actually used.

My suggestion is lets just add those which are applicable to the current MR.
Done

😞
It *was* a move in the right direction.. and it reflects the Privilege models that we *should* be adhering to.  
That's OK, priv checking updates will be in the upcoming plan, we will need to work this again soon.
It fetches detailed privilege information for each role, but this data is stored in rolePrivileges state which is never actually used.
Done
Looks good to me, Thanks for addressing the comments.
